fees.flatDesc: Used when custom geographic pricing is off, and for locker delivery.

deliveryPricing.title: Custom geographic delivery pricing
deliveryPricing.desc: Optional distance-based home delivery pricing. Leave this off to keep your existing delivery fees.
deliveryPricing.enableHelp: Replaces the flat home delivery fee with county/distance rules. Locker delivery is unchanged.
deliveryPricing.originMissing: No pickup/business address configured yet. Add it in eAWB shipping settings.
deliveryPricing.originHelp: Distance is calculated from your existing eAWB pickup/business address.
deliveryPricing.noRules: No rules yet. Add at least one rule before customers can check out with this method.
deliveryPricing.localityPlaceholder: Leave empty to apply to the whole county
deliveryPricing.priceHelp: Delivery price = this amount × quantity ordered.
deliveryPricing.rulesHelp: Rules that share an area cannot overlap. Touching brackets such as 0–30 and 30–100 are allowed.
deliveryPricing.errMax: Maximum distance must be greater than minimum distance.
deliveryPricing.errOverlap: This rule overlaps another rule for the same area.
deliveryPricing.errCounty: Select a county when adding a locality-specific rule.
deliveryPricing.ownDesc: You deliver orders yourself. Set where you go, how far, and how the fee is calculated.
deliveryPricing.providerHelp: Courier shipping with eAWB, or your own van / bike / in-house delivery.
deliveryPricing.modeDistanceHelp: Charge a fee for each distance band, for example 0–10 km = 20 RON.
deliveryPricing.modeOrderHelp: Charge a fee based on the cart total, for example under 100 RON = 25 RON, over 200 RON = free.
deliveryPricing.modeCombinedHelp: Use distance fees, then replace them when an order-value rule matches (typical for free delivery over a threshold).
deliveryPricing.maxDistanceHelp: Leave empty for no km limit. Addresses farther than this are rejected.
deliveryPricing.originOwnHelp: Distance and coverage are measured from this address.
deliveryPricing.noOrderRules: No order-value rules yet. Add a catch-all such as 0+ RON.
deliveryPricing.maxOrderHelp: Leave empty for no upper limit.
deliveryPricing.flatFeeHelp: This is the trip fee for that distance, not multiplied by product quantity.
deliveryPricing.errMinOrder: Minimum order value cannot be negative.
deliveryPricing.errMaxOrder: Maximum order value must be greater than the minimum, or empty.
deliveryPricing.errOrderOverlap: This order-value rule overlaps another rule.
deliveryPricing.chargeTransportHelp: One fee for the whole delivery, no matter how many items. Example: 50 RON for the trip.
deliveryPricing.chargeItemHelp: Fee × quantity. Example: 50 RON per pallet, 3 pallets = 150 RON.
deliveryPricing.feeTransportHelp: Customers pay this once per order.
deliveryPricing.feeItemHelp: Customers pay this amount for each item in the cart (for example each pallet).

netopiaSetup.title: Setup Payments
netopiaSetup.subtitle: Securely connect your Netopia account in just a few minutes.

errors.openBrowserFailed: Could not open Netopia. Please try again.

1.title: Create or log into your Netopia account
1.description: You need a Netopia merchant account before you can accept online card payments.
1.helpExplanation: Open Netopia in a secure browser window, create an account or sign in, then return here to continue.
1.tip1: Use the same email you use for your business.
1.tip2: Make sure your Netopia account is activated before continuing.
1.tip3: You can reopen Netopia anytime from this step.

2.title: Create a Point of Sale (POS)
2.description: Inside Netopia, create a new Point of Sale for your website.
2.helpExplanation: A POS represents your online store in Netopia. Create one for your SpeedVendors storefront, then open Technical Settings.
2.tip1: Choose a clear POS name that matches your store.
2.tip2: Website / e-commerce POS type is usually the right choice.
2.tip3: You will need Technical Settings in the next steps for your signature.

3.title: Copy your API Key
3.description: Find your API Key under Security → API and paste it below.
3.helpExplanation: In the Netopia admin dashboard, open Security → API, then generate or copy your API Key.
3.tip1: Make sure your account is activated.
3.tip3: Generate a new key if necessary. Sandbox and Live keys are different.

4.title: Copy your POS Signature
4.description: Find your POS Signature under Point of Sale → Technical Settings.
4.helpExplanation: Open your POS Technical Settings and copy the Signature value (often formatted like XXXX-XXXX-XXXX-XXXX).
4.tip1: Select the POS you created for this store.
4.tip3: Copy the Signature exactly — do not add spaces.

5.title: Verify connection
5.description: Confirm your credentials, then connect Netopia to SpeedVendors.
5.helpExplanation: We will securely test these credentials against Netopia, then save them to your store profile.
5.tip1: Double-check you did not mix Sandbox and Live credentials.
5.tip2: If the test fails, go back and re-copy your keys.
5.tip3: Advanced options (Public Key, Sandbox/Live) are available in Settings after setup.

success.title: Netopia connected successfully
success.description: Your store is now ready to accept online card payments.

1.title: Create or log into your eAWB account
1.description: An eAWB account is required before generating shipping labels.
1.helpExplanation: Open eAWB, create an account or sign in, then activate your merchant account before continuing.
1.tip1: Open eAWB in a secure browser window.
1.tip2: Log in or register with your business email.
1.tip3: Make sure your account is activated before generating an API key.

2.title: Generate and paste your API Key
2.description: Create an API key in eAWB, then paste it below. We save it securely to your store profile.
2.helpExplanation: In the eAWB dashboard, open Settings → API, generate a key, and paste it here. Continuing saves the key to your profile so the next steps can retrieve addresses.
2.tip1: Save your key somewhere safe — you may not see it again.
2.tip2: The key must be saved before retrieving addresses.
2.tip3: If retrieve fails, confirm the key was generated for an activated account.

3.title: Retrieve Pickup Addresses
3.description: This is where couriers will collect your parcels. Select a pickup address from your eAWB account.
3.helpExplanation: We use the same Europarcel pickup address retrieval already available in Settings. Create a shipping address in eAWB first if the list is empty.
3.tip1: Create at least one shipping/pickup address in your eAWB dashboard.
3.tip2: Click Retrieve Pickup Addresses, then select one.
3.tip3: This address is used when generating AWBs without a locker pickup.

4.title: Retrieve Billing Address
4.description: Select the billing address linked to your eAWB account.
4.helpExplanation: We use the same billing address retrieval already available in Settings.
4.tip1: Create a billing address in eAWB if none appear.
4.tip2: If you only have one, it may be linked automatically.
4.tip3: You can change this later in Advanced Settings.

5.title: Default Pickup Locker (Optional)
5.description: If you regularly ship from a courier locker instead of your warehouse, choose your default pickup locker.
5.helpExplanation: This reuses the same locker picker as Settings. The locker is suggested when creating AWBs and can always be changed per shipment.
5.tip1: Skip this step if you only ship from a warehouse address.
5.tip2: Use Map, List, or Locate Me to find your locker.
5.tip3: You can update the default locker anytime in Advanced Settings.

6.title: Test Connection
6.description: Verify that SpeedVendors can reach your eAWB account with the saved credentials.
6.helpExplanation: This runs the same connection test already used in Settings. No new API is introduced.
6.tip1: Ensure your API key was saved in step 2.
6.tip2: If the test fails, go back and re-check your key.
6.tip3: Carrier and service defaults remain optional in Advanced Settings.
